new_case_groups.purpose: Role identity, privilege and deployment registry
new_case_groups.target: Four role OIDs/names, function ACL, deployment/build/worker-principal registration
new_case_groups.method: Inspect fixed expected signatures/privileges, use real SCRAM logins and wrong or absent credentials; recreate a role OID and attempt membership/name drift. The SCRAM fixture also opens a new correct-password dispatcher connection and confirms an absent-password connection fails immediately after HBA reload and before yielding to the test. The same test explicitly checks table-level and every-column profile_catalog UPDATE denial plus DELETE denial for runtime, operator, dispatcher and projector, then issues real WHERE-false UPDATE/DELETE statements as each service principal and requires InsufficientPrivilege.
new_case_groups.pass_criteria: Only the intended role can execute each security-definer function; invalid identity/membership/OID drift is rejected atomically; trust-local fallback cannot authenticate service roles. No runtime, operator, dispatcher or projector can directly UPDATE any profile_catalog column or DELETE catalog rows; only the trusted owner-import boundary can maintain that immutable source.
new_case_groups.expected: Role scopes and owner-registered immutable deployment/build identity match the approved H2 contract.

new_case_groups.purpose: Initial activation SQL and receipt/run fences
new_case_groups.target: G4 create receipt, workspace readiness, dispatcher reserve/start/admit/delivery, projector activation and receipt replay
new_case_groups.method: Create through the actual G4 HTTP service, seed only required owner fixtures, connect with separate SCRAM dispatcher/projector principals, and call the versioned SQL API with literal wrong-token/generation/run cases. It also changes the workspace generation after reserve/admission for one pending accepted job and verifies quarantine/no activation, while a separate already-committed receipt still replays after a later workspace-generation change. Independently rebuild the exact 18 immutable binding fields and versioned SHA-256, then exercise real HTTP list/detail/command DTOs and idempotent POST replay before and after inserting a profile-less future human command and revoking current membership.
new_case_groups.pass_criteria: Valid DTO reserves and binds one execution; stale claim/run/workspace fences cannot apply; DRAFT revision 0 becomes QUEUED revision 1 exactly once; exact already-committed scoped projector receipt replays unchanged after mutable user authority is revoked. The start-window binding tuple begins all-NULL; partial population is rejected by the named binding_start_window_shape CHECK without changing the tuple, while the valid operation atomically records the complete tuple. A new pending job with a changed READY workspace generation is quarantined with WORKSPACE_IDENTITY_CONFLICT and retains DRAFT0, accepted command and zero receipts; an existing exact applied receipt remains replayable after the same identity change. The returned binding hash equals the digest of the independently constructed 18-field canonical document. While active, list/detail show the create command profile version and QUEUED1 state exactly once; command GET shows applied1 and POST same key/body returns the original accepted receipt. Once membership is revoked, external detail/command GET and POST replay are forbidden while only the internal machine-scoped receipt replay remains allowed.
new_case_groups.expected: Accepted, dispatched and applied remain separate states; no implicit later workflow step or human result is produced.

new_case_groups.target: B01 snapshot profile_version behavior through actual G4 HTTP acceptance and H2 SQL activation
new_case_groups.method: Use the real pinned Node snapshot builder/bridge to publish and capture an additional profile for the existing scalar project_id with profile_version U+D800. Independently assert the escaped profile_version_json and snapshot bytes, import/grant the resulting catalog record, submit an ASCII-escaped CreateJob body through the real G4 API, then run dispatcher claim/reserve/start/admit/delivery and projector read_activation/project_activation using separate SCRAM principals. Keep the normal frozen-clock G4 eligibility grant for the HTTP acceptance and insert a second owner-controlled SQL grant bounded around actual PostgreSQL clock_timestamp() for SQL activation; the two clocks are intentionally distinct.
new_case_groups.pass_criteria: The pre-existing B01 bridge behavior is preserved: the lone-surrogate profile label round-trips as U+D800 while its JSON label and record use the exact escaped form. Actual G4 returns 202, and the H2 projector applies once, yielding QUEUED revision 1 for the same job and payload digest. project_id remains a Unicode-scalar string.
new_case_groups.expected: A profile_version accepted by the existing snapshot bridge and G4 create path remains eligible for the real SQL activation path; no surrogate is silently normalized or causes catalog identity quarantine.
evidence: Independent B01 bridge invariants: exact profile_version_json and escaped record bytes.
Real G4 HTTP 202 accepted receipt and independently computed canonical create-envelope SHA-256.
Real dispatcher/projector function results and final job/command/binding/receipt rows proving one QUEUED revision 1 application.
Separate synthetic G4 frozen-clock and SQL wall-clock eligibility rows, with no modification to either time oracle.
